title: Bumba and the missing hat.
lines: In a big circus, with a red and white striped tent, lives a little clown.
His name is Bumba.
Bumba has a red nose, big shoes and a happy laugh.
Hee hee hee!
Every evening Bumba does a show for all the children.
He does tricks, he juggles balls and he falls on his bottom.
Plop!
And then all the children laugh.
But one morning something is wrong.
Bumba is looking for his hat.
His lovely hat with a flower on it.
He looks under his bed.
No hat.
He looks in the cupboard.
No hat.
Oh dear, oh dear, says Bumba.
The show is tonight, and I don't have a hat!
Bumba goes searching around the circus.
First he goes to the elephant.
The elephant is big and grey, with a long trunk.
Elephant, have you seen my hat?
The elephant shakes his big ears.
No, Bumba, but I'll help you look!
With his long trunk he looks high up in the tree.
No hat.
Then they go to the seal.
The seal can spin a ball on its nose.
Seal, have you seen my hat?
Ork, ork, says the seal.
No, but I'll help look too!
They look in the big barrel of water.
Splash!
No hat.
Then they hear something.
Squeak, squeak, squeak!
It's coming from the dressing-up trunk.
Bumba opens the trunk very carefully.
And what does he see?
His hat!
And in the hat three little mice are sleeping, snuggled up close together.
A mummy mouse looks at Bumba, scared.
Sorry, Bumba, says the mummy mouse.
My babies were cold, and your hat is so soft and warm.
Bumba smiles.
He doesn't want to wake up the mice.
He thinks.
Then he has an idea!
He takes an old sock, a soft, striped sock, and he makes it into a little bed.
Very carefully he lays the mice in the sock bed.
They just keep on sleeping.
Snore, snore.
Thank you, Bumba, says the mummy mouse.
In the evening the show begins.
Drum roll!
Bumba comes on with his lovely hat.
The elephant sprays water with his trunk.
The seal spins the ball.
And Bumba does his very best trick: he lifts his hat, and there are the three mice sitting on his head!
They wave their little paws.
All the children clap and laugh.
Hooray for Bumba!
And from that day on the mice are in the show every evening.
